image_query: Standing Buddha Mathura red sandstone Kushan period sculpture
tweets: The Mathura school gave the Buddha his first native Indian face. Carved from warm, lichen-flecked red sandstone, this Kushan-era image (2nd century CE) stands broad-shouldered, right hand raised in abhaya mudra, robe clinging in schematic folds — utterly human.

Mathura's workshops carved for every faith at once — Buddhist, Jain and Hindu images from the same red-stone quarries near Sikri. Here, alongside Gandhara, India's own sculptors first gave the Buddha a body. Follow @yddoseOfHistory for your daily dose of history
